- [USER] The user discusses legal matters related to a Tribunal's findings regarding a construction contract.

- [USER] The user mentions that the builder did not cite Butler v Fairclough in post-hearing submissions but cited Haller instead.
- [USER] The user states that the Tribunal was not obliged to provide more detailed reasons than those given.
- [USER] The user outlines Grounds 6 and 7 concerning the completion date of works under a 2009 contract.
- [USER] The user indicates that Ground 6 involves whether the Tribunal erred in finding the completion date was 20 October 2010.
- [USER] The user explains that Ground 7 questions whether leave to appeal should be granted based on the Tribunal's finding being against the weight of evidence.
- [USER] The user quotes the Tribunal's statement regarding practical completion occurring on 20 October 2010 when the Final Occupation Certificate (FOC) was issued.
- [USER] The user discusses the definition of "building works" in the contract, emphasizing the importance of legal approval for occupation.
- [USER] The user notes that the Tribunal's reasoning included that the builder was responsible for obtaining the FOC.
- [USER] The user explains that the Tribunal's conclusion about completion date is a question of law and that leave to appeal is not required for Ground 6.
- [USER] The user states that the Tribunal's finding regarding the completion date was relevant to its finding of consideration in respect of a new contract.
- [USER] The user concludes that the Tribunal erred in its interpretation of relevant terms of the contract.
- [USER] The user provides the definition of "building works" from Clause 1 of the contract.
- [USER] The user explains the meaning of "practical completion" as defined in the contract.
- [USER] The user cites Clause 7 of the contract regarding planning and building approvals, stating that the builder is responsible for obtaining them.
- [USER] The user references Clause 26 of the contract regarding progress payments and the final progress claim.
- [USER] The user argues that the Tribunal erred in finding that the FOC was part of the definition of "building works."
- [USER] The user asserts that the receipt of the FOC is not necessary for the building works to be reasonably capable of being used for their usual purpose.
- [USER] The user concludes that the Tribunal erred in its interpretation of the contract regarding the completion date of the works.
- [USER] The user states that this conclusion makes it unnecessary to consider Ground 7.
